$$r=n-(c+2e+q+t)\ge0.$$

$$\#\{x\notin S\cup W\}\le r.$$

$$n=5c+2s+q+t+r.$$

$$\boxed{n\ge5c+3s+q+2d+r.}$$

Both additional remainder coefficients are exactly correct.In particular, (A) implies
$$r\le\eta.$$
Also, the original first inequality establishes

There is no hidden assumption that the remainder is zero.1.3 Minimum-degree edge capacityThis is the essential new argument.Consider a selected isolate  $i$  with  $h(i)=1$ .Because  $i$  is a selected isolate:
$$N(i)\cap S=\varnothing.$$

$$(\delta-1)a
\le
\sum_{i:h(i)=1}
|N(i)\setminus(S\cup W)|.$$
Each unused outside vertex has degree at most  $\Delta$ . Therefore
$$\sum_{i:h(i)=1}
|N(i)\setminus(S\cup W)|
\le
\Delta\,|V(G)\setminus(S\cup W)|.$$
Since the number of unused outside vertices is at most  $r$ ,
$$\boxed{(\delta-1)a\le\Delta r.}
\tag{C}$$

$$2d\le a+b_2+b_3-s$$
